coverage.description: Read the complete current article, every standard pair and inline construction. Assessed pronunciation, morphology/history, all meanings and major coverage, argument roles, separability, selected lexical relations, natural English/Japanese, register and ordinal per-sense scores. Independently compared the 54 original English examples as a multiset: none missing. Inspected all source facts and the full claim-to-source-ID map. No B report or author verdict was read.

focus_notes: The ten learner units separate departure, reflexive/causative movement, removing people from roles/equipment, and withdrawing services from physical removal and numerical subtraction. These differences concern actual subject/object roles and meanings. Flight/jump departure is explicitly defined and illustrated, without confusing ordinary human departure with flight.

The noun takeoff/take-off material is clearly labelled as related-noun usage, including a correctly framed a takeoff of example and a new during-takeoff pair. The current phrasal-verb entry need not reproduce every specialist noun submeaning.

The displayed verb and noun stress distinction is accurate. The noun examples of US/UK vowel notation are labelled examples; they do not claim that every American speaker has only the displayed /ɔː/ realization.

The core omission does not erase useful lexical coverage. A physical-separation mnemonic could help several branches, but presenting imitation as extraction of features or inventing a homograph/exclusion category would misteach the modern system. The explicit histories and construction-specific explanations are a defensible treatment under v5. No absent core area was claimed freshly checked.
The source-supported older copy/reproduce history is distinguished from a speculative contemporary derivation. The genuine late Old English stage is retained with Scandinavian origin.

Pronoun position, noun-object separation, off complements and reflexive constructions are explained through actual frames. A literal-headword classifier is not sufficient reason to reject inflected/separated phrases or examples with a genitive object.

The temporal-break versus record-reduction distinction no longer relies on quantity alone. State/action and contextual comparisons are labelled; the free paraphrases retain their examples without lexical-looking scores.
Current regional, medical and aviation notes stay lexical. No medical decision rule, legal guarantee or flight procedure is inferred from an example.

The independently read FAA runway passage supports broader verb lift-off usage. This supplements the narrower typical-rocket/helicopter dictionary presentation and does not require calling the previous vertical association fictitious.

No concrete residual requiring correction was found in this snapshot. Scores were judged as global-English ordinal estimates for the stated senses; no empirical frequency measurement or fine numerical tuning was imposed.
